issues.title: Filled triangle line ends are also stroked with the line pen (miter), so heads grow by ~1.6 line widths and the tip overshoots the end point
issues.description: 144 findings on 116 slides, every one a type="triangle" tailEnd (no other line-end types or headEnds occur among the findings). Line widths and sizes: 2.25 pt med/med (40, e.g. slides 9-22, 78-105, 158-176), 3 pt med/med (23: 13 straight lines, 6 custGeom bezier freeforms, 4 prstGeom arc), 3 pt lg/lg (36, slides 118-150, 598, 632-633, 810-812), 4.5 pt med/med default w/len (43, the timeline arrow on slides 578-648, 390, 174-175), 0.75 pt med/med (2, slides 29 and 32, the thin-line minimum). All fit one model exactly: Euro-Office draws PowerPoint's correctly sized triangle, then strokes its outline with the full line pen and miter joins. The outline adds (1/cos a + tan a) x w = 1.618 w to the base width and to the length (a = 26.57 deg half-angle of a 3x3 or 5x5 head), puts the tip 1.118 w past the end point and moves the base w/2 back. Measured (coverage-weighted width profiles in the 1600-px renders, sheet px): 4.5 pt line (w=5.0 px) slide 578: PowerPoint head 14.7 wide x 14.85 long, tip at 748.1 (end 748.3); Euro-Office 22.9 x 23.1, tip 753.7 (predicted 23.1 x 23.1, tip 753.9). 3 pt lg/lg (w=3.33) slide 120: 16.5 vs 21.8-22 px, tip 3.8 px past (predicted 22.1, 3.7). 3 pt med: 9-9.6 vs 14.5-14.8 (predicted 15.4). 2.25 pt med (w=2.5): 7.4 vs 11 px, tip 2-2.8 px past (predicted 11.55, 2.8). So the size ratio is 1.55x at med and 1.3x at lg only because the constant 1.618 w excess is a smaller share of a 5 w head. Curves (custGeom, arc) are the same: head direction matches PowerPoint, only the size and overshoot differ. 0.75 pt lines: both apps apply a minimum base width (PowerPoint about 2.0 pt: head 6.7 x 6.7 px on slide 29 connector 20; Euro-Office 2.5 px at 96 dpi = 1.875 pt), and the 0.83 px outline makes Euro-Office's head 7.6 px and the tip 0.9-1.3 px past the end, i.e. 1.15x, the same mechanism at smaller magnitude.
issues.powerpoint: Fills the line-end polygon only, no outline. Triangle head = width x length of sm 2, med 3, lg 5 times max(line width, about 2 pt) (0.7 mm, the floor LibreOffice's OOXML import also uses), tip exactly on the path end point, and the shaft is shortened under the head so a thick line's butt end never shows beside the tip (sharp tip even on 4.5 pt lines).
issues.euro_office: Builds the same polygon (tip on the end point, base len back, width w), fills it, then strokes the same closed polygon with the line pen; the arrow pass leaves the pen join at miter. The head grows by w/2 on every side: base width and length +1.618 w, tip 1.118 w past the end point, base w/2 further back. The shaft is stroked full length to the end point and is only hidden by the inflated head. Thin-line floor is 1.875 pt instead of about 2 pt.
issues.suspected_cause: DrawLineEnd's Triangle case fills (drawer.drawStrokeFillStyle) and then strokes (drawer.ds) the head polygon; the stroke uses the line's own pen width and, because CShapeDrawer.ds/drawFillStroke skip Ln.Join while IsArrowsDrawing, a miter join. The other closed line ends (Oval, Stealth, Diamond, Square, ReverseTriangle) use the same fill-then-stroke pattern, so they should be oversized the same way, although this deck has none.
issues.code_area: sdkjs word/Drawing/ShapeDrawer.js: DrawLineEnd (41), case AscFormat.LineEndType.Triangle (431-483): fill at 472, second _s/_m/_l/_z + drawer.ds() stroke at 475-481 (same fill-then-stroke pattern in Diamond 113, Square 171 (232/262), Oval 266 (318/331), Stealth 335 (364/373), ReverseTriangle 378 (419/427)); CShapeDrawer.drawArrows (1623): head size from EndArrow.GetLen/GetWidth (common/Drawings/Format/Format.js 7337/7392: 2/3/5 x max(penWidth, min)), minArrowSize = 2.5 / g_dKoef_mm_to_pix mm (1.875 pt) in PDF mode (1643-1645); the shaft is stroked full length before drawArrows in CShapeDrawer.ds (2194) / drawFillStroke PDF branch (2560), path emitted by Path.prototype.drawSmart / Path2.prototype.drawSmart (common/Drawings/Format/Path.js 1627 / 3102).
issues.fix_idea: 1) In DrawLineEnd, for Triangle (and the other filled closed ends: Stealth, Oval, Diamond, Square, ReverseTriangle) drop the second polygon + drawer.ds() and only fill (keep the PDF-editor colour fix-up for the fill). 2) Because the head is no longer inflated, the shaft's butt end would poke out beside the tip on thick lines (for med it shows within w of the tip), so shorten the stroked path at each end that has a filled line end: before stroking, move the first/last point of the first/last open subpath back along the path by about len/2 (head length converted to path units with transformScaleFactor; len/2 is always inside the head since width >= 2 x max(w, min)), while drawArrows keeps using the original end point and direction for the head. Alternatively clip the shaft stroke with the head polygon. 3) Optional, for thin lines: raise the PDF-mode floor minArrowSize from 2.5 / g_dKoef_mm_to_pix (1.875 pt) to 0.7 mm (about 1.98 pt) so 0.75 pt heads come out 6.7 px instead of 6.25 px after step 1 (residual about 0.45 px at 80 dpi otherwise). Check: slide 578 head should become 15 x 15 px with the tip at x 748.3, slide 120 16.7 x 16.7 px with the tip at y 130.0, slide 29 connector 20 about 6.7 x 6.7 px with the tip at x 269.4.
issues.fixed_in: sdkjs 44cdab9e9f (fix(slide): draw triangle arrowheads like PowerPoint)

log.note: Fixed in word/Drawing/ShapeDrawer.js (+ Geometry.js draw/drawSmart), presentation editor only: 1) DrawLineEnd's Triangle case only fills the head (no second stroke of the polygon with the line pen). 2) The shaft is shortened under each triangle head: CShapeDrawer.getPathsToDraw trims the first/last open subpath (lines and cubic beziers, cut where the path crosses a circle around the end point) so the stroke ends (len - s/2) before the tip, s = max(line width, 2 pt), i.e. s/2 past the head's base, which is where PowerPoint's PDF ends it; drawArrows still uses the untrimmed end point and direction. Filled paths keep their full outline for the fill. 3) PDF-mode floor raised from 1.875 pt to 2 pt (minArrowSize = 2 x 25.4 / 72 mm). Checked in the PDFs against PowerPoint's: page 578 (4.5 pt med/med) shaft end 662.229, head base 659.979, tip 673.479, half-width 6.75 pt, all equal to PowerPoint's; page 120 lg/lg head 15 x 15 pt; pages 29 and 32 (0.75 pt) heads 6.0 x 6.0 pt; the curved shaft on page 593 matches. Harness run k1-filled-heads vs i012-pic-outline-outside: lines 96.7% -> 96.7%, identical slides 673 -> 673, SSIM 0.9575 -> 0.9576; 115 slides better and 0 worse on SSIM. Of the 116 slides with findings, 115 are better, 1 unchanged at 4 decimals (32, a single 0.75 pt head), 0 worse. Not changed: the other closed line ends (Stealth, Oval, Diamond, Square, ReverseTriangle; none in this deck) and the screen-mode floor.

issues.title: Glyph advances use exact linear design widths, but PowerPoint lays text out with its own quantised per-glyph advances, so long lines drift and borderline words wrap differently
issues.description: This is the K2 mechanism, here at more than 2 px. Line breaks match, but glyphs drift steadily along long lines. Regular Calibri at 13.5-18 pt ends 2.0-3.2 px early on 540-760 px lines (about 0.3-0.4% short, about 0.03 px per character). Bold 13.5 pt ends 1.5-2.5 px late (slides 541, 550/551, 631), while bold 12 pt ends about 2 px early (24, 192). URLs with many narrow glyphs drift faster (0.52%). 30 findings on 28 slides. A numeric check (work-glyphs-fonts/roundtest3.py, roundtest4.py, model-check.txt; calibri.ttf/calibrib.ttf hmtx+kern) shows that Euro-Office's line ends equal the exact sum of design advances plus kern pairs. For example, slide 97 'according to ... into' predicts an ink end of 774.1 px, and EO measures 774.0. PowerPoint's lines match a model where each glyph's advance is rounded to whole 1/576-inch units (ppem = pt x 8) and the kern adjustment is truncated toward zero. On 18 test lines that model predicts PPT-EO end offsets of +2.6/+2.5/+2.7/+2.1/+1.2/+3.7/+2.6 px (regular 18 pt; measured +3.0/3.0/3.0/3.0/1.5/3.0/2.5), +1.1/+0.8/+1.5/+1.7 (regular 13.5 pt; measured 2.0/2.0/1.5/3.0), -2.0 (bold 13.5 pt; measured -1.5), +2.8/+2.9 (bold 12 pt; measured +2.0/+2.0) and +1.8/+2.6/+1.9 for the three URLs (measured 2.0/2.5/2.0). RMS error is 0.70 px, against 2.5 px for linear advances. The model also gets the sign flip between bold 12 pt and bold 13.5 pt right, which no constant scale factor can. Not fully explained: small extra steps at run boundaries (slides 48 and 110, where PowerPoint's text after a colour-run change is up to 1 px wider than the same text in one run), and about 0.4 px at a baseline=30000 superscript (slide 509).
issues.powerpoint: Lays out glyphs with advances quantized to its 576-dpi master-unit grid. Each glyph advance at ppem = 8 x pt is rounded to an integer, and pair kerning is applied as a truncated integer number of units. As a result line lengths deviate from linear design widths by a weight- and size-dependent amount: +0.35-0.4% for regular Calibri at 13.5/18 pt, -0.3/-0.5% for bold at 13.5 pt, +0.4% for bold at 12 pt.
issues.euro_office: Shapes text with HarfBuzz at 576 pt (FONTSIZE in engine.js) and scales the 26.6 advances linearly to the run size. Advances are therefore exact, unquantized design widths plus kerning, and the per-glyph rounding bias PowerPoint accumulates is missing.
issues.suspected_cause: Euro-Office measures slide text with the font's exact linear advances: HarfBuzz at MEASURE_FONTSIZE 576, scaled to the run size, with spaces from GetGraphemeWidth (engine.js HB_ShapeString, TextShaper.FlushGrapheme/private_HandleSpace). PowerPoint lays text out with per-glyph advances that differ from the linear hmtx widths by small amounts that depend on the glyph, size and weight. Where breaks match, this shows as drift: regular Calibri 13.5/18 pt about +0.35% wider in PowerPoint, bold 13.5 pt the other way (K2 tags; 30 findings over 2 px). On lines that end within that margin of the text edge, one word moves (91 findings in wrap-k3/1). EO's line is 0.26-2.6 pt narrower on the regular lines where it fits an extra word, and 0.7-2.1 pt wider on the bold lines where it fits one fewer. The best model so far rounds each advance to whole 1/576-inch units at the run size and truncates kern values. It gives RMS 0.70 px on 18 test lines, against 2.5 px for linear advances, and it matches the 13.5 pt regular space (grid 3.000 vs 2.997 pt measured). It does not match all of wrap-k3/1's per-glyph PDF data: the 13.5 pt bold space measures 2.78 pt against 3.00 predicted. The fixed 0.25 pt PRESENTATION_LINE_WIDTH_REDUCTION (Shape.js 4085) only compensates the regular-weight drift on average, and it must be re-fitted once the advances change (see K3).
issues.code_area: sdkjs/common/libfont/engine.js: AscFonts.HB_ShapeString (554), where `nWidth += x_advance * COEF` (598) yields the width per 1 pt of font size; sdkjs/word/Editor/Paragraph/TextShaper.js: CParagraphTextShaper.FlushGrapheme (178), where `_nWidth` (202) is passed to private_HandleItem -> CRunText.SetWidth (word/Editor/Paragraph/RunContent/Text.js:295), which multiplies by the font size
issues.fix_idea: For slide (presentation) text only, quantize each grapheme's advance at the run's real size. Let u = 25.4/576 mm. Then width_mm = round(nominalAdvance_mm / u) * u + trunc(kernDelta_mm / u) * u. Do this in CParagraphTextShaper.FlushGrapheme, or pass the size into HB_ShapeString, and divide back by FontSize before SetWidth, because SetWidth stores per-pt widths times FontSize. The nominal advance is the glyph's hmtx advance (from an unkerned measurement via AscFonts.GetGraphemeWidth of a single-glyph grapheme). The kern delta is x_advance minus that nominal value. A simpler first try is round((advance+kern)/u)*u (RMS 1.15 px on the same lines, versus 0.70 for the full model and 2.5 today). Validate on the whole deck: the K2 drift tags and the K3 wraps should both shrink.

merged_from.title: Line breaking uses the font's nominal advances, but PowerPoint lays text out with its own per-glyph advances, so borderline words wrap differently
merged_from.description: 91 findings on 90 slides: one line of a paragraph breaks one word later or earlier than in PowerPoint, and the paragraph reflows from there (often several lines, sometimes the whole rest of the paragraph; on S0235, S0288, S0601, S0603 and S0604 the paragraph loses a line and everything below moves up 18 px, on S0114, S0335 and S0534 it gains one that is drawn outside the stored spAutoFit box). Measured exactly from both PDFs (glyph positions from the content streams, text edge from the XML): Euro-Office's own line is narrower than PowerPoint's on the same words in all regular-weight cases where it fits one more word (13.5 pt: 43 lines, median 0.69 pt, range 0.26-1.8 pt; 18 pt: 31 lines, median 1.44 pt, range 0.82-2.6 pt), and 0.7-2.1 pt WIDER in the bold cases where it fits one fewer word (S0054, S0114, S0163, S0187, S0317-2, S0335, S0534, S0552, S0630, S0677, S0838; median 0.90 pt) and in three space-heavy regular lines (S0084, S0324, S0764; 0.24-0.31 pt). Euro-Office's glyph positions themselves match the font's nominal advances (hmtx + kern table at the run size) to within -0.1..-0.35 pt per full line; it is PowerPoint that departs from the font metrics. S0510/S0525 additionally have a superscript 'th' that Euro-Office sets at 11.5 pt (18 x vaKSize 0.65, rounded to a half point in CRunText.SetMetrics) and that the reviewer measured about 0.4 px shorter than PowerPoint's; S0202 is 9 pt bold, where PowerPoint is wider than nominal (+1.5 pt).
merged_from.powerpoint: PowerPoint places glyphs with advances that differ from the font's hmtx by small per-glyph, per-size and per-weight amounts and breaks the line on that measure. From its PDF (k==0 pairs only): 13.5 pt regular Calibri letters +0.018 pt each on average (+0.13% em; e.g. 'o' 7.187 vs 7.119 pt, 'h' 7.119 vs 7.093) and spaces -0.055 pt (2.997 vs 3.052); 18 pt regular letters equal hmtx (-0.002%) but spaces +0.04..+0.07 pt (modes 4.068/4.176/4.212 vs 4.069); 13.5 pt bold letters +0.03..+0.04 pt and spaces -0.27 pt (about 2.78 vs 3.05 pt; 18 pt bold -0.14 pt); 9 pt bold spaces +0.12 pt. Net: a full 13.5 pt regular line comes out +0.3..+0.6 pt wider than nominal, an 18 pt regular line +0.7..+1.8 pt wider, a 13.5 pt bold line -0.5..-2.2 pt narrower. Its break decisions follow these rendered widths (PowerPoint's own line would overflow the text edge by 0.0-1.7 pt in the regular cases it wraps; its accepted bold lines end 0.08-0.85 pt inside the edge).
merged_from.euro_office: Euro-Office shapes with HarfBuzz at AscFonts.MEASURE_FONTSIZE (576) and scales the unhinted design advances linearly to the run size (spaces from GetGraphemeWidth), i.e. it uses the font's nominal metrics, then compares against the box width minus insets minus a fixed 0.25 pt + 0.01 mm. A fixed width offset cannot match a difference that is proportional to line length and changes sign with weight and size, so regular 13.5/18 pt lines fit an extra word and bold lines lose one.
merged_from.suspected_cause: Advance-width model mismatch (the K2 drift mechanism): PowerPoint's layout advances are not the linear hmtx widths. The per-glyph deltas recur for a given glyph and size (e.g. 'n' alternates 7.119/7.065 pt at 13.5 pt, steps of ~0.05-0.06 pt), which points to advances quantised on a layout grid / grid-fitted at PowerPoint's internal resolution, with space widths treated differently per weight; the exact rule is not yet identified. The 0.25 pt PRESENTATION_LINE_WIDTH_REDUCTION was fitted to compensate the regular-weight drift on average.
merged_from.code_area: word/Editor/Paragraph/TextShaper.js: CParagraphTextShaper.FlushGrapheme (178) and private_HandleSpace (296) set item widths from HarfBuzz/GetGraphemeWidth; common/libfont/textshaper.js: CTextShaper.FlushWord (96) shapes at AscFonts.MEASURE_FONTSIZE = 576 (common/libfont/engine.js:413); widths stored by CRunText.SetWidth (word/Editor/Paragraph/RunContent/Text.js:295) / CRunSpace.SetWidth (Space.js:139); fit test in ParaRun.Recalculate_Range (word/Editor/Run.js:3868, 3949: X + SpaceLen + WordLen + LetterLen > XEnd); compensation in CShape.recalculateDocContent (common/Drawings/Format/Shape.js:4081-4085, constant at 970).
merged_from.fix_idea: Derive PowerPoint-compatible advances for slide text: build a table of PowerPoint's effective advance per (font, weight, size, glyph) from its PDF exports (pdfglyphs.py/pptadv.py in grouping/work-wrap-k3 extract them) and test candidate rules against it (e.g. advances grid-fitted at a fixed layout ppem, per-weight space width); apply the rule in private_HandleSpace/FlushGrapheme for presentation shapes only (so drawing and line breaking stay consistent), then re-fit or remove PRESENTATION_LINE_WIDTH_REDUCTION. As a cheaper interim step, a per-weight correction of the space advance (13.5 pt bold space -0.27 pt, regular -0.055 pt, 18 pt regular +0.06 pt) would already move most of these lines. Also set superscript size like PowerPoint (about 2/3 of the base size, not rounded to a half point).

merge_notes: wrap-k3/1 names its own cause as 'the K2 drift mechanism', and the K2 issue says the same drift 'sometimes flips a borderline wrap'. Both locate it in the same code (TextShaper.FlushGrapheme / private_HandleSpace, engine.js HB_ShapeString, CRunText.SetWidth) and propose the same fix: PowerPoint-compatible per-glyph advances for presentation text. The wrap findings are lines where the drift crosses the text edge; the K2 findings are lines where it does not. The sign pattern is the same in both (regular narrower, bold 13.5 pt wider). The merged issue should keep wrap-k3/1's major severity (121 findings). It should also use both data sets (work-glyphs-fonts/roundtest3-4.py and work-wrap-k3/pptadv.py) to validate the advance rule. wrap-k3/1's S0510/S0525 also carry part of the vertical/5 superscript-size error.
doubts: The 1/576-inch per-advance rounding model fits the K2 line ends (RMS 0.70 px) and the regular 13.5 pt space, but not all of wrap-k3/1's per-glyph PowerPoint PDF data. At 13.5 pt the bold space measures 2.78 pt (model 3.00), the bold letters measure +0.03..+0.04 pt (model about -0.01), and regular 'o' measures 7.187 (model 7.125). Treat the rule as a hypothesis: validate it against both data sets before coding it, especially bold. Note also that PowerPoint's PDF sets 13.5 pt text at Tf 13.56 or 13.584, varying per line (page 125), so any analysis that uses PDF font sizes instead of glyph positions will be biased.
issues.fixed_in: sdkjs e84bfe4efb (fix(slide): lay slide text out in 1/576-inch units like PowerPoint)

log.note: Hypothesis checked on PowerPoint's PDF (all 838 pages) before coding; scripts and outputs in review/grouping/work-glyphs-fonts/k2-layout-check (k2starts.py: word starts, k2words.py: within words). PowerPoint uses two grids. (1) Layout: the start positions of words along a line (so line widths and line breaks) follow the 1/576-inch model with S pt = 8 x S units per em (13.5 pt -> 108): each glyph's own advance rounded to a whole unit (halves up), spaces included, and pair kerning added UNROUNDED. Word-start residual (PowerPoint minus model), mean and slope: regular 13.5 pt -0.015 pt, -0.006 pt per 100 pt (100588 word starts); bold 13.5 -0.011, -0.007 (5233); regular 18 -0.11, -0.03; bold 30 -0.01, -0.006; regular 10.5 (kerning off at < 12 pt) -0.015, -0.006. Exact design widths: +0.10, +0.047 (13.5); +0.64, +0.21 (18); -0.41, -0.32 (bold 13.5). The issue's variant with the kerning truncated toward zero is rejected: -0.24, -0.10 at 13.5 and -0.44, -0.14 at 18 (rounded kerning comes close to exact). (2) Drawing: the PDF's font size is the run size rounded to 1/600 inch (13.56, 12.72, 39.96, 44.04) and the glyphs inside a word sit at 600-dpi rounded advances (76% of 13.5 pt words within 0.03 pt of that model, 23-26% for linear or 1/576 widths); the spaces absorb the difference, so word starts follow the layout grid. This is why per-glyph and within-word measurements pointed at 600 dpi and line ends at 576. Two measurement traps on the way: PowerPoint's TJ adjustments are sparse, so single-glyph advances are biased, and a parser bug (Tc kept across Q) made the 10.5 pt list text on 627-648 look 0.5 px per glyph wide. Regular 12.75 pt fits less well (-0.17 pt, -0.06 per 100 pt), bold 12.75 fits (-0.03, -0.02). Fixed in word/Editor/Paragraph/TextShaper.js, presentation editor, baseline text: the unkerned advance of each single-glyph grapheme (measured before shaping and cached per font and glyph, because the font engine cannot be called while the shaped glyphs are read) is rounded to 1/8 pt at the run size and the shaper's kerning is added back; spaces are rounded the same way. word/Editor/Paragraph/RunContent/Space.js now keeps fractional sizes for spaces as CRunText does (a 12.75 pt space was measured at 13 pt). Measured together with K3. Harness run k2-k3-layout576 vs k1-filled-heads: lines 96.7% -> 99.6% (14903 -> 15346 of 15410), identical slides 673 -> 774, SSIM 0.9576 -> 0.9834; line breaks 109 slides better and 0 worse; SSIM 828 better and 4 worse: 255 (-0.0068; regular 12.75 pt lines now end about 0.45 pt late where linear widths ended about 0.2 pt early on average, breaks unchanged; the other 12.75 pt slides 85, 478, 684, 685, 692, 693, 700 improved), 496, 203, 308 (0.0005 or less). All 116 K2 slides better, 110 now break exactly like PowerPoint (26 before); still different: 35, 93, 116, 510, 525, and 163 with every line matched. K2 alone with K3's 0.25 pt reduction kept (run k2-adv-576): 97.8%, 706 identical, SSIM 0.9789, but 54 slides worse on line breaks than k1-filled-heads, so the two only work together.

The four slides that still broke some lines differently after K2 and K3: 116 lacked a break after an en dash (I-022), and 510 and 525 had superscripts drawn too small (I-010). All three now match PowerPoint. On 93 Euro-Office keeps 'like' at the end of a line where PowerPoint wraps it. In Euro-Office's layout that line ends less than 0.01 pt inside the text width, and at PowerPoint's own drawn positions it would fit too. So this is K2's residual, not a separate rule, and it is left as is.

The 1646-slide deck has much more text at other sizes (6342 long lines at 18 pt, and 17, 20, 25, 26 and 32 pt) and shows that PowerPoint's line lengths depart from this model by size and from line to line, by up to about 2 per mille; Euro-Office follows the model exactly. Opened as I-027.

issues.title: Words that end within a few tenths of a point of the text edge: Euro-Office's fixed 0.25 pt line-width reduction rejects words PowerPoint keeps
issues.description: 13 findings where Euro-Office breaks one word EARLIER although its glyph positions on the line agree with PowerPoint's to within about 0.15 pt (or are narrower): bullets on the same box at three widths (S0011/S0013/S0014: 'Ephraim.', 'God'), quote lines (S0316 'ye', S0353 'the', S0386 'hastens', S0729 'to', S0775 'it', S0590/S0591/S0592 'somewhat'), the bold 18 pt oval labels (S0390 'Israel.') and the 22.6 pt-wide 'Lud' label (S0440, which Euro-Office then splits inside the word, Lu/d, because a single word that does not fit is broken by character). Every following line of the paragraph reflows; on S0390 the extra line overflows the 35 px oval and on S0440 'd' hangs below the white box.
issues.powerpoint: PowerPoint keeps the word when its own rendered line ends between 0.35 pt inside the text edge (box minus lIns/rIns) and slightly past it: measured PowerPoint margins +0.35 (S0353), +0.30 (S0316, S0386), +0.20 (S0590-S0592), +0.15/-0.04 (S0011), +0.07 (S0013/S0014), +0.06 (S0729), -0.15 (S0390), -0.94 pt (S0775). Its tolerance is not a fixed width: in other boxes it wraps words whose rendered line would end 0.26-0.37 pt inside the edge (S0093, S0486, S0502, S0297, S0721), so its break measure is not exactly its rendered glyph positions.
issues.euro_office: Euro-Office lays slide text out on (box width - insets - 0.25 pt - 0.01 mm). On these lines its own line with the extra word would end 0.06-0.31 pt inside the text edge (S0440: 0.12 pt; S0390: about 0.1 pt past), i.e. inside the box but inside the 0.278 pt reduction zone, so the word is moved to the next line.
issues.suspected_cause: The constant PRESENTATION_LINE_WIDTH_REDUCTION (0.25 pt, plus TEXT_RECT_ERROR 0.01 mm) added in commit 7898a3e is a statistical compensation for the advance drift of wrap-k3/1; on lines without drift it makes Euro-Office stricter than PowerPoint. Without it, 12 of these 13 lines would match (all but S0390). PowerPoint's own acceptance band (-0.94..+0.37 pt) overlaps with its rejection band, so these are genuinely borderline and no single constant reproduces all of them.
issues.code_area: common/Drawings/Format/Shape.js: CShape.recalculateDocContent (4081-4085: oContentW -= TEXT_RECT_ERROR + PRESENTATION_LINE_WIDTH_REDUCTION; constant at 970); fit test in word/Editor/Run.js ParaRun.Recalculate_Range (3868, 3949); mid-word split in Paragraph.FindLineBreakInLongWord (word/Editor/Paragraph_Recalculate.js:2723) called from Run.js:3899.
issues.fix_idea: Fix wrap-k3/1 first, then re-fit the reduction against PowerPoint's PDF line ends: with PowerPoint-compatible advances the measured accept/reject margins suggest a much smaller value (about 0-0.1 pt) instead of 0.25 pt. Removing the reduction on its own fixes these 12 lines but, per the commit message, costs about 1.5% of matched lines elsewhere because the advance drift is then uncompensated, so do it together with wrap-k3/1. For single words wider than the line in tiny label boxes (S0440), consider letting a word that overflows by less than the reduction stay whole rather than splitting it by character.

merged_from.title: A single word that fits a narrow box is split mid-word, because the fixed 0.25 pt line-width reduction makes it too wide
merged_from.description: Slide 176 Rectangle 33 (also slide 440, filed as K3 S0440-1): the red bold 13.5 pt label 'Lud' in a 26 px wide box is drawn 'Lu' / 'd', the 'd' hanging below the box over a connector. PowerPoint keeps the word on one line. Text area = 299259 - 2 x 20574 EMU = 20.32 pt; 'Lud' needs about 20.20 pt (Calibri Bold 3064/2048 em), so it fits with 0.13 pt to spare. issues.title: Underline and strikethrough position and thickness are hard-coded instead of taken from the font's post/OS2 metrics (underline about 0.6 px high and 0.1 px thin; strike about 1 px high; bold strike not thicker)
issues.description: Underlines sit about 0.6 px higher and are about 0.1 px thinner than PowerPoint's (1600 px renders). Recorded as a slide tag.

merged_from.title: Strikethrough uses a fixed 0.27 em position and fontSize/18 thickness instead of the font's OS/2 strikeout metrics (about 1 px too high, not thicker for bold)
merged_from.description: On slide 96 (TextBox 4, every run strike=sngStrike, Calibri 18 pt) all five strikes sit 0.95-1.2 px higher in Euro-Office. The regular strikes are 1.2 px thick against 1.4 px. On the bold line 'Acts 3:22-23' EO keeps the thin 1.25 px stroke where PowerPoint draws about 2 px, so EO's strike runs above the en dash instead of through it. Calibri's OS/2 table gives yStrikeoutPosition = 512 (the top of the stroke) and yStrikeoutSize = 134 (regular) or 186 (bold), out of 2048 units. At 18 pt (20 px/em) that puts the stroke centre 4.35 px above the baseline with a thickness of 1.31 px (regular) or 1.82 px (bold), which matches PowerPoint. EO's 0.27 em is 5.40 px, about 1.05 px higher. This is probably the same family as K4 (underline about 0.6 px high and thin), which uses the post table's underlinePosition/underlineThickness in PowerPoint.
merged_from.powerpoint: Places and sizes the strikethrough from the face's OS/2 metrics: stroke top at yStrikeoutPosition, thickness yStrikeoutSize. The bold face has a larger yStrikeoutSize, so bold text gets a thicker strike.
merged_from.euro_office: Draws the strike centred at baseline - 0.27 x font size, with thickness fontSize/18 pt, for every font and weight.
merged_from.suspected_cause: Hard-coded strike geometry in the paragraph line-drawing state. No font metrics are consulted.
merged_from.fix_idea: For slide text, get the run's actual face (with bold/italic) from the font manager and read the OS/2 yStrikeoutPosition/yStrikeoutSize. Set strikeoutY = baseline - (yStrikeoutPosition - yStrikeoutSize/2)/upem x size, and the strike width = yStrikeoutSize/upem x size. Fall back to 0.27 and size/18 when the metrics are missing. Using post.underlinePosition/underlineThickness the same way for the underline would likely also fix K4.

issues.suspected_cause: ParagraphLineDrawState.updateStrikeoutUnderlinePos (word/Editor/Paragraph/draw/line-draw-state.js 544-569) places the strike at 0.27 em above the baseline. It places the underline at UnderlineOffset = 0.4 x line TextDescent (word/Editor/Paragraph.js 3169), and gives both the same thickness lineW = fontSize/18 pt. PowerPoint uses the face's own metrics: the underline top at post.underlinePosition with thickness about post.underlineThickness (Calibri -232/134 units), and the strike from OS/2 yStrikeoutPosition/yStrikeoutSize (Calibri 512/134, Calibri Bold 512/186). PDF page 125 (13.5 pt Calibri, baseline 342.86): PowerPoint fills the underline band 340.50-341.34, i.e. top 1.52 pt below the baseline (post predicts 1.53) and 0.84 pt thick (post 0.88). Euro-Office strokes 0.75 pt centred at 341.44, which is 0.52 pt (0.58 sheet px) higher and 0.09 pt (0.1 px) thinner: exactly the K4 tag. The strike in S0096-2 is 1 px too high and not thicker for bold, for the same reason.
merge_notes: K4 and glyphs-fonts/5 are set in the same function, which shares one lineW between strike and underline, and both are explained by the same missing input, the font's decoration metrics. The PDF check above shows that post.underlinePosition/underlineThickness reproduce K4's sign and size (0.6 px higher, 0.1 px thinner). OS/2 yStrikeout* reproduce the strike offset and the bold thickness in glyphs-fonts/5. One change makes the function read the face's post/OS2 decoration metrics (with the current constants as fallback) and fixes both; glyphs-fonts/5 already proposes it.

issues.title: Pictures are written to PDF as tiling-pattern fills instead of clipped image draws, so they are resampled more smoothly than PowerPoint's and their edge rows/columns are under-painted
issues.description: A picture in the same place and size is interpolated slightly more smoothly than PowerPoint's. Recorded as a slide tag.

merged_from.title: Pictures are exported as tiling-pattern fills, so their edge rows and columns are under-painted
merged_from.description: 22 findings on 22 slides: a 1-px row or column along a picture edge is lighter or almost empty in Euro-Office. (a) The full-bleed photo on slides 37-46 (right edge 799.59 px) leaves column 799 at RGB about 231-240 instead of picture colour. That is about 10% coverage, while the column is 59% covered by the geometry and PowerPoint paints it fully. (b) The image60 photo on slides 669-673 and 680-682 (bottom edge 367.52 px) leaves row 367 at about 2% coverage (mean 251 vs 56-68). (c) On slides 408/409, 467 and 684 the edge rows of photos are 30-70% covered where PowerPoint paints them fully. This happens even at an edge that falls exactly on a pixel boundary (slide 408 top edge y 425.00: 70%). On slide 467 it also shows at 1600 px (column 1379 at an exact x 1380.0 edge: 75%). Most cases only show at 800 px; the 1600-px renders usually match. Each case loses about 0.3-0.5 px of coverage at the edge. The result is a faint light line along the photo edge.
merged_from.powerpoint: Its PDF draws every picture as a clipped image XObject: 'q x y w h re W* n  w 0 0 h x y cm /ImageN Do Q'. The rasterizer (Windows.Data.Pdf, used for both PDFs) snaps image XObject edges to whole device pixels by rounding each edge. Slide 37: x 0.41 -> 0 and 799.59 -> 800, so columns 0-799 are solid. At 1600 px: 0.82 -> 1 and 1599.18 -> 1599. Slide 680: bottom 367.52 -> 368.
merged_from.euro_office: Its PDF paints every picture as a path fill with a tiling pattern. Slide 37: '/Pattern cs /P1 scn 0 540 m 719.26549 540 l ... f', where P1 is PatternType 1, XStep = 2 x width (1438.53), BBox = the image plus a half-width transparent margin on each side, and the tile content is '719.26549 0 0 387.29707 0 0 cm /X1 Do'. A sample of every 7th page of the Euro-Office PDF has 94 pattern fills and no direct image draws. The path geometry is exact (x 0.36731-719.6328 pt = 0.41-799.59 px; slide 680 y 126.45-367.52 px), so sdkjs does not mis-round the rectangle (the reviewers' round(x)+round(w) theory). The rasterizer renders the pattern tile on its own grid and blends the image's outer pixels with the tile's transparent margin, so the edge rows and columns come out partly transparent.
merged_from.suspected_cause: In PDF/renderer mode, CImageShape.draw sends the blip through ShapeDrawer as a texture brush: put_brushTexture(src, 0) + put_TextureBounds + drawpath(256). CDocumentRenderer records that as a texture-brush path fill, and core's PDF writer (x2t) turns a texture brush into a tiling pattern instead of a clipped image draw. The pattern path is rasterized differently from PowerPoint's image XObject at the picture edges.
merged_from.code_area: sdkjs word/Drawing/ShapeDrawer.js: drawFillStroke (line 2264). Its isPdf() branch sets the texture brush at 2311-2366 (put_brushTexture 2320/2336, put_TextureBounds 2338/2365) and fills with drawpath(256) at 2545. It is called from common/Drawings/Format/Image.js: CImageShape.prototype.draw (lines 642-643). The renderer side is common/Drawings/Metafile.js: CDocumentRenderer.prototype.put_brushTexture (3388). CDocumentRenderer.prototype.drawImage (3278) and StartClipPath/EndClipPath (3477/3485) already exist and write ctDrawImageFromFile. The pattern itself is built in core's PdfWriter (not sdkjs; not located).
merged_from.fix_idea: In ShapeDrawer.drawFillStroke, when isPdf() && bIsTexture && fill.tile == null (stretch) and the fill is opaque, replace the texture fill with SaveGrState(); clip to the geometry path (AddClipRect for IsRectShape/prstGeom rect; otherwise StartClipPath + the path + EndClipPath); Graphics.drawImage(src, texX, texY, texW, texH, alpha, srcRect) using the same texture bounds (fillRect/srcRect) under the current shape transform; RestoreGrState(). Then stroke the outline as before. The PDF then holds 're W n ... cm /Im Do' like PowerPoint's, and the rasterizer snaps the picture to whole pixels. Keep the pattern path only for tiled blips (fill.tile set). To check: re-render slides 37, 408, 467 and 680 and compare column 799, row 425 and row 367.

issues.suspected_cause: Confirmed: core's PDF writer, not sdkjs. sdkjs sends a picture as a path filled with a texture brush over the picture's rect; CPdfWriter::UpdateBrush turned every texture brush into a tiling pattern, and CPdfWriter::LoadImage encoded every picture as a JPEG at quality 85.
merge_notes: Tested by rewriting Euro-Office's own PDF (work-merges/pat2img.py). On pages 39 and 106 the '/Pattern cs /P1 scn <rect> f' fill was replaced with a clipped direct draw of the same /X1 image, then rasterized with fidelity/windows/pdf-to-png.ps1. Inside the picture, the mean absolute difference to PowerPoint's render drops from 3.10 to 1.23 levels (p39) and from 4.84 to 1.07 (p106) at 1600 px. On p106 the pixels more than 16 levels off drop from 7.5% to 0.05%, and the max difference from 200 to 23. On the K6 note's border rows on p106, PowerPoint reads 0,0,41,214,214,255; the pattern gives 0,29,42,162,215,243 and the direct draw 0,0,42,215,215,255. The same rewrite also removes the pictures-misc/1 edge defect. p39 column 799 at 800 px: pattern 234, direct 30, PowerPoint 30. p106 bottom row 829 at 1600 px: pattern 210, direct 116, PowerPoint 115. So the one change pictures-misc/1 proposes (drawImage under a clip instead of the texture-brush pattern for stretched, untiled blips) fixes both.
doubts: After the direct-draw rewrite a residual of about 1 level remains (max 23). On page 106 Euro-Office embeds the PNG picture (media/image14.png) as DCTDecode (JPEG), while PowerPoint keeps it lossless (FlateDecode, /Interpolate false). That lossy re-encode is probably in core's PDF writer (x2t), not in sdkjs, and is a separate small issue.

Two of the deck's 65 media that PowerPoint keeps at full size do not follow the encoding rule: image54 (29 x 27, 547 colours with alpha: Flate 1721 bytes against JPEG 906) and image34 (116 x 173, 2105 colours: Flate 10265 against JPEG 2855) are lossless in PowerPoint's PDF, and Euro-Office writes them as JPEG. issues.powerpoint: Draws each picture as an image XObject clipped to its shape ('q <path> W* n  w 0 0 h x y cm /ImageN Do Q'), one XObject per medium (and per crop) shared by every page that shows it. A cropped picture's image holds only the part shown (srcRect l 10%, t 20%, r 5%, b 15% of a 320 x 200 picture: a 272 x 130 image). Every picture is re-encoded, a JPEG too: lossless (Flate of the RGB, no predictor, /Interpolate false) when it has at most 256 colours or when JPEG would not make it smaller, otherwise JPEG at quality 75 (the Windows codec: entropy data identical to GDI+ at quality 75, plus a 92-byte Exif segment; 4:2:0, /Interpolate true). Transparency (the picture's alpha times alphaModFix) is a soft mask (Flate, DeviceGray, /Matte [0 0 0]) with the colour premultiplied by it. Images drawn on their own (the blurred shadows of I-014) follow the same rule. Tiled picture fills are tiling patterns, one tile per step. Pictures drawn above about 270 dpi are downsampled (I-025).
issues.euro_office: Before the fix: painted each picture as a path filled with a tiling pattern (PatternType 1, XStep and YStep twice the picture's size, a transparent margin of half its width and height around the image), which Windows' renderer resampled on the tile's own grid: the picture came out smoother than PowerPoint's and its edge rows and columns partly transparent (slide 37's column 799 at 800 px: 239 against PowerPoint's 81). Every picture that was not a JPEG became a JPEG at quality 85 (IJG tables), a JPEG was passed through and a cropped picture was embedded whole. issues.description: Every run whose rPr sz is not a multiple of 50 is laid out and drawn at the nearest half point. issues.title: Kerning pairs that involve the space glyph are never applied (Times New Roman 'space A', 'space T')
issues.description: Slide 1's 96 pt Times New Roman title line 'Of All Things' (spc=-300, kern=1200 from the master title style) is 7.5 px wider in Euro-Office. The gap 'Of'->'A' is 29 vs 23 px and 'All'->'Things' is 32.5 vs 31 px, so 'Of' sits 4 px left and 'Things' 3.5 px right on the centred line. times.ttf has kern pairs space+A = -113 and space+T = -37 units (-5.89 and -1.93 px at 96 pt, -7.81 px in total), which matches the measured 7.5 px. The first title line, which has no space pairs, matches exactly. Calibri has no space pairs, so the Calibri body text is unaffected, but Times New Roman and Arial text (both have space pairs) will show this whenever kern applies.
issues.powerpoint: Applies the font's pair kerning across spaces (space+A, space+T, A+space and so on) when the run size is at or above the kern threshold.
issues.euro_office: Flushes the shaping buffer at every space and measures the space on its own with its plain advance, so no kern pair with a space as either glyph is ever applied.
issues.suspected_cause: CParagraphTextShaper.HandleRun treats a space (a non-text item) as a word boundary: it calls FlushWord() and then private_HandleSpace, which takes the bare glyph advance. HarfBuzz never sees the (prev, space) or (space, next) pairs.
issues.code_area: sdkjs/word/Editor/Paragraph/TextShaper.js: CParagraphTextShaper.HandleRun (141, the `!oItem.IsText()` branch that does FlushWord + private_HandleSpace) and private_HandleSpace (293)
issues.fix_idea: When the run is kerned (TextPr.IsKerned()), add the kern pairs on both sides of the space to the space's width. Look up kern(prevGlyph, space) and kern(space, nextGlyph) from the font (HarfBuzz hb_font_get_glyph_h_kerning, or by shaping a 3-glyph string prev+space+next and taking the space's advance delta). Fold both into the space item's width in private_HandleSpace. Keeping spaces as separate items preserves line breaking and justification. The same lookup is needed at run boundaries where the font stays the same.

log.note: Fixed in the presentation editor, in four parts. (1) The theme's supplemental fonts (<a:font script typeface>) are read (BinaryPPTYLoader.ReadFontCollection record 3) and kept in FontCollection.scriptFonts. (2) A run's theme cs font (+mn-cs, +mj-cs) resolves, when the theme leaves the cs typeface empty, to the script font for the run's language: he-IL -> Hebr, ar-SA -> Arab, th -> Thai, hi -> Deva and so on (FontScheme.checkSlideCSFont, AscFormat.getComplexScriptForLanguage). x2t writes an empty theme typeface as "Arial", so a cs of "Arial" counts as empty when the theme has script fonts; a theme that really sets cs to Arial would get the script font instead (PowerPoint's themes leave cs empty). (3) In slide text, complex-script characters (Hebrew, Arabic, Syriac, Thaana, Indic, Thai, Lao, Tibetan, Khmer and their presentation forms) use the cs font, as in PowerPoint, instead of the ASCII slot Word gives Hebrew and Arabic without RTL or cs. Spaces, punctuation and other neutral characters use the cs font too in runs whose language is a complex-script one, unless a letter of another script comes before them in the run (CParagraphTextShaper.GetFontSlot, private_HandleSpace). (4) The garbled Hebrew had a second cause, independent of the font, which already existed in release 9.3.8: for right-to-left text HarfBuzz returns the glyphs in visual order, but the code points were handed out in logical order. Each glyph therefore carried another letter's code point, and the PDF is drawn from those code points (repeated shin, missing lamed, detached marks). CCodePointsCalculator now walks the clusters backwards for RTL runs (common/libfont/engine.js), and a cluster with several glyphs matches each glyph to its code point through the font's cmap (grapheme.js FillCodePointsByCmap). Test deck script-font-rules (work folder decks/script-font-rules, make_script_font_deck.py and font_per_case.py). Its theme maps Hebr to Times New Roman and Arab to Courier New, so each source is visible. he-IL Hebrew and he-IL Arabic both use the Hebr font: the language decides, not the letters. ar-SA Hebrew and ar-SA Arabic use the Arab font. en-US Hebrew uses Arial for the letters and Calibri for the spaces. he-IL Latin stays Calibri. Spaces inside a he-IL run use the Hebr font. The fonts now match PowerPoint in all 9 boxes, SSIM 0.9948. Slide 674: the Hebrew is now in Arial, in visual order and with its marks, and the Latin text on that line stays Calibri. The fallback-font spill came from the missing Hebrew font and is gone. issues.title: An a:ln with no w (and no p:style lnRef) is stroked at 12700 EMU (1 pt) instead of PowerPoint's 9525 EMU (0.75 pt)
issues.description: The most common outline difference in the deck: 153 findings on 136 slides (6-225, 410-420, 585-648, 682-706); part 2 counted 436 such objects on 191 slides. Every affected object has <a:ln> with only a solidFill (no w attribute) and no p:style/lnRef: mostly the black outlines of the yellow FFFFCC/FFFF99 quote and label boxes, the white Tithes/Fast Offerings labels, red frames on 201-205 and 8 pictures. Euro-Office strokes them 1.33x too wide. Both PDFs go through the same aliased rasterizer (Windows.Data.Pdf, fidelity/windows/pdf-to-png.ps1), which lights a device pixel when its centre is inside the stroke, so a 2.22-px stroke (1600-px render) lights 2-3 rows or columns where PowerPoint's 1.67-px stroke lights 1-2; at 800 px an edge on a pixel boundary becomes 2 px instead of 1. Which edges differ depends only on where each edge falls on the pixel grid, which is why reviewers first called it 'snapping' and why each finding names only some edges. Pixel snapping is NOT a separate cause. Re-checked in the PDFs (pages 86, 114, 213, 417, 633, 702): PowerPoint writes '0.75 w' and Euro-Office '0.99998 w' for exactly these outlines. A 0.5 pixel-centre coverage rule from the xfrm reproduces every PowerPoint edge with 0.75 pt and every Euro-Office edge with 1 pt at 800 and 1600 px (S0114-2, S0148-2, S0120-2). Rotated, antialiased boxes integrate to 1.11-1.12 vs 0.83-0.84 sheet px (= 12700/9525, slides 632/633). Same-geometry outlines with an explicit w=9525 match pixel for pixel (slides 141-147, 417, 586, 634; Euro-Office's PDF writes '0.74999 w' there). Group scaling plays no part (704/706). The only 'snapping' leftovers are two exact pixel-centre ties decided by PowerPoint's PDF rounding coordinates to 0.01 pt (rejected S0332-1, S0402-1). Effect: some frame edges are 2-3x heavier, visible at 800 px (e.g. S0031-1, S0086-2, S0119-2).
issues.powerpoint: An <a:ln> with no w and no style lnRef is drawn at 9525 EMU = 0.75 pt: its PDF writes '0.75 w' (with '1 j') for every such outline checked (pages 6, 86, 88, 114, 188, 191, 201-225, 410-420, 597-648, 682-706). That is 1.67 device px at 1600 px wide (5715 EMU/px) and 0.83 px at 800 px. With a p:style lnRef the theme lnStyleLst width applies (idx 1 = 9525; idx 2 = 25400 gives '2 w' on slide 701 even though spPr a:ln has no w), and Euro-Office already gets that case right.

issues.suspected_cause: CShape.prototype.recalculatePen leaves pen.w null when there is no p:style lnRef and spPr.ln has no w (pen = new CLn() merged with the compiled line). CShapeDrawer.fromShape (called by fromShape2) then substitutes 1 pt: 'this.StrokeWidth = (this.Ln.w == null) ? 12700 : parseInt(this.Ln.w)'. The same 12700 default is repeated in the other consumers of pen.w: the bounds checker, the shadow shape's pen padding, Word-shape insets, hit testing, ShapeToImageConverter and the asc stroke object shown in the UI.

Pen compiled in common/Drawings/Format/Shape.js: CShape.prototype.recalculatePen (line 3121), also used by pictures via common/Drawings/Format/Image.js: CImageShape.prototype.recalculatePen (line 362). Same 12700 fallback in common/Drawings/CommonController.js: CSlideBoundsChecker.prototype.CheckLineWidth (10450), common/Drawings/Format/GraphicObjectBase.js: recalculateShdw (1198), Shape.js 4657 (bWordShape insets) and 6460 (hit test), ShapeDrawer.js 2659 (ShapeToImageConverter), common/Drawings/Format/Format.js 16836 (asc stroke width for the UI) and slide/Editor/Format/Slide.js 1952 (commented out).

issues.title: When no line join is specified (in a:ln or the theme line style), Euro-Office strokes with a miter join; PowerPoint uses a round join
issues.description: 18 findings on 18 slides (187-193, 201-206, 243, 585, 676, 679, 701). Affects every outline whose a:ln and referenced theme lnStyleLst entry have no <a:round/>, <a:bevel/> or <a:miter/>. theme1 has no join in any line style, and the only explicit join anywhere in the slide XML is <a:miter/> (189 occurrences). On rectangles it shows as square, filled outer corners where PowerPoint draws an arc of radius w/2: the thick red 3 pt and 4.5 pt frames on 187-193 (1.7-2.5 sheet px radius), and the 1.5-3 pt frames on 243 and 585 (trivial); see crop grouping/work-outlines/0188-corner.png. On acute vertices it shows as miter spikes. The yellow leftArrow heads (1.5 pt) on 201-206 get back-corner spikes about 1 px further out, and the tip moves 0.5 px. The rtTriangle with a 4.5 pt line on 676/679 gets a tip 2.5-4 px beyond PowerPoint's rounded corner. Each of the eleven foldedCorner fold vertices on 701 (2 pt, 31-degree angle) gets a 2.5 px barb. Line widths and positions match.
issues.powerpoint: An outline whose join is not given (in its a:ln or in the theme line style its lnRef names) is stroked with a round join: the PDF writes '1 j' before the stroke. That holds for 156 of the 187 presets, custom geometry, connectors (straight, bent and curved), text boxes, shapes in groups and picture outlines. The other 31 presets (bentUpArrow, chevron, cube, downArrow, ellipseRibbon, ellipseRibbon2, leftArrowCallout, leftRightArrowCallout, leftUpArrow, mathEqual, mathMinus, mathMultiply, mathNotEqual, mathPlus, moon, notchedRightArrow, plus, quadArrowCallout, rightArrow, star4, star5, star8, star10, star12, star16, star24, star32, stripedRightArrow, upArrow, upDownArrow and upDownArrowCallout) are stroked with a miter join, also when the XML says <a:round/>; flipping, rotating, the line width (0.75-6 pt), a dash, no fill, a text box or a group do not change that. <a:bevel/> gives a bevel join ('2 j') and <a:miter/> a miter join (no 'j') on every preset. The miter limit is never written (the PDF default, 10), whatever a:miter/@lim says (800000 and 100000 tested); a theme line style with <a:miter lim="800000"/> gives a miter join. Lines with arrowheads are filled outlines in the PDF, not strokes; their bent shafts have round corners unless the join is miter. Measured on two test decks built for it: linejoin-rules (all 187 presets with no join, 6 presets with 8 join variants, 32 other cases) and linejoin-rules2 (the 31 mitered presets with <a:round/> and <a:bevel/>, 16 round ones with <a:miter/> and <a:bevel/>, 28 lines and connectors with arrowheads).
issues.euro_office: Before the fix: every stroke in its PDF had a miter join ('0 J 0 j 10 M'), an explicit round or bevel join included. On screen an outline with no join was mitered (the canvas default); an explicit join was used. On the 838-slide deck 1518 of the strokes paired with PowerPoint's were mitered where PowerPoint's are round, on 239 slides; the 268 strokes PowerPoint miters matched.
issues.suspected_cause: Confirmed: ShapeDrawer used the join only when the a:ln or the theme line style gave one, so an unspecified join fell through to the canvas or PDF default (miter), and the PDF branch of drawFillStroke never passed a join to the writer, because OldLineJoin is only set when there is a canvas context. PowerPoint's per-preset exception (31 presets mitered even when the join is round) was not known when the issue was opened; the rightArrow on slides 207 and 701 was the one case seen.
issues.code_area: word/Drawing/ShapeDrawer.js: CShapeDrawer.checkSlideLineJoin, called from draw with the geometry being drawn, and SLIDE_MITER_JOIN_PRESETS; ds uses LineJoinType for the canvas, and drawFillStroke's PDF branch passes it to the writer with put_PenLineJoin and puts the writer back to miter after the path.
issues.fix_idea: Both changes are needed, or the PDF output stays mitered. (a) In CShape.prototype.recalculatePen, after pen.merge, if this.pen.Join is null (or its type is null), set it to a LineJoin of type AscFormat.LineJoinType.Round (or treat null as Round inside ShapeDrawer). (b) In ShapeDrawer, decouple the PDF path from m_oContext: compute joinType in fromShape regardless of the graphics object, save and restore m_oContext.lineJoin only when a context exists, and in drawFillStroke's PDF branch always call this.Graphics.put_PenLineJoin(AscFormat.ConvertJoinAggType(joinType)), plus the miter limit when a:miter lim is given. Afterwards check: slide 188 (round frame corners); slides 201, 676, 679 and 701 (spikes gone); slide 141 (explicit miter stays miter); and the rightArrow on 207 and 701, which PowerPoint miters and may need a preset-specific exception.

Scaled font sizes agree (15 pt and 28 pt in both PDFs), and at 100% spacing first baselines agree to 0.01 pt (e.g. slide 718).
issues.powerpoint: Under percentage spacing other than 100%, and under exact spacing, a line is H high: the percentage of the text height (1.2 x the font size; the tallest text on a mixed line) or the exact value in whole points. A quarter of H lies below the baseline, plus however much the font's single-spacing descent exceeds a quarter of the single line height (Courier New); at single height or less the part below is never more than the font's descent. The rest lies above. 18 pt Calibri (single line 21.6 pt, descent 4.75): at 150% the first baseline is 24.3 pt below the box top (0.75 x 32.4), at 200% 32.4, at 80% 12.96 (a quarter, 4.32, is less than the descent), at 90% 14.69 (a quarter, 4.86, is more, so all 2.16 pt come off above). Exactly 100% keeps the font's own ascent (16.85), so 101% puts the first baseline about 0.5 pt higher than 100% does. Exact 22 pt spacing: 16.5. normAutofit lnSpcReduction is subtracted from the percentage, also from lnSpc set on the paragraph itself (100% - 20% = 80%, 150% - 20% = 130%); exact spacing is not reduced. For ctr and b anchoring (and the text height) the last line ends at its font descent below the baseline; the rest of its line height is not counted. PowerPoint then snaps baselines to a 1/600-inch grid, so single cases differ by up to 0.12 pt.
issues.euro_office: Before the fix: Word's rule. Above 100% the text kept its single-spacing ascent and the extra went below each line, so the first baseline stayed at the 100% position (18 pt Calibri: 7.6 pt too high at 150%, 15.6 at 200%). Below 100% the whole reduction came off above the line (0.44 pt too high at 80%, 2.1 at 50%). Exact spacing put the whole difference above the baseline (5.2 pt too low at 40 pt). The last line's extra space counted in the text height, so ctr- and b-anchored 18 pt text at 150% sat 9.3 and 11.0 pt too high. lnSpcReduction applied only to inherited spacing, not to lnSpc set on the paragraph.
issues.suspected_cause: Confirmed: Euro-Office placed lines under line spacing by Word's rule (the text keeps its ascent and the whole difference goes below the line above 100%, above it below 100%, and above the baseline under exact spacing), counted the last line's extra space in the text height, and ignored lnSpcReduction when lnSpc was set on the paragraph itself.

issues.powerpoint: Each run on a line takes 1.2 x its own size, split above and below the baseline at its font's win ascent : win descent (I-016). The a:br that ends the line adds its own font at the size of the line's last run, and so does the paragraph mark on the last line when the paragraph has an a:endParaRPr (even one that names no font; with no endParaRPr the mark does not count). The a:br's and endParaRPr's own sizes do not count, and a bullet's font does not count at all. The line takes the largest part above the baseline and the largest part below it and scales both down together to 1.2 x its largest run size. So 18 pt Calibri (16.85 above, 4.75 below) with an Arial run (17.50, 4.10) is 17.50 + 4.75 = 22.25 scaled to 21.6: the baseline 16.99 pt below the line top (PowerPoint 17.05 on its 0.12 pt grid), and the line is no taller than an all-Calibri line. With Courier New (15.87, 5.73) the baseline rises to 16.12 (PowerPoint 16.14). A smaller run in another font counts at its own size: 24 pt Calibri with a 22 pt Courier New run gives 21.97 (PowerPoint 21.97); with a 20 pt run nothing changes. Line spacing other than 100% (I-017) then works on these parts. issues.title: The TrueType fonts in Euro-Office's PDF have a cmap that runs past its end, so Windows draws their text with system fonts and a composed bet with dagesh loses its dot
issues.fixed_in: core 2d4497c536 (fix(PdfFile): write the subset cmap's entryCount as the codes it holds)
issues.description: Found while fixing I-006, not by the review. Slide 674: the he-IL word בַּז (bet, dagesh, patah, zayin) is drawn in Arial since I-006, but in Euro-Office's PDF the bet has no dagesh dot; PowerPoint's has it. HarfBuzz composes bet + dagesh into one glyph (Arial's U+FB31). Euro-Office's PDF maps that glyph to both code points in ToUnicode, as it should, yet the shape drawn is the plain bet. Shin + shin dot (U+FB2A) is composed the same way on this line and may lose its dot too (not checked).
issues.powerpoint: Draws the bet with its dagesh (one glyph in its PDF, which ToUnicode maps to plain bet).
issues.euro_office: Before the fix: drew the composed bet + dagesh glyph as plain bet, and shin + shin dot (U+FB2A, on the same line) as plain shin. The PDF holds the right glyphs; Windows' PDF renderer (Windows.Data.Pdf, which the harness rasterizes with) rejected every font embedded in it and drew the text from ToUnicode in a system font, one character per glyph.
issues.suspected_cause: Confirmed, and not the one first suspected: the PDF writer picks the right glyph id. core's CFontFileTrueType::WriteTTF writes each embedded subset's cmap as one format-6 subtable (platform 1, encoding 0) whose entryCount is always 256, while the subtable holds one entry per code the subset uses (its length is 10 + 2 x codes). A subset with fewer than 256 codes therefore has a cmap that claims entries past its own end. Windows rejects such a font, and its PDF renderer then draws the text from ToUnicode with a system font, one character per glyph, so a glyph that stands for several characters (bet + dagesh, shin + shin dot) is drawn as its first character alone. Euro-Office embeds one subset per font for the whole document; all 5 in the 838-slide deck's PDF (Calibri, Calibri Bold, Calibri Italic, Times New Roman, Arial: 20 to 105 codes each) were rejected. Setting only entryCount in that PDF made Windows draw the embedded fonts, the dagesh and the shin dot.

issues.powerpoint: Lays text out with K2's model and draws it in I-027's glyph runs, but places each glyph on its 600-dpi device and has its PDF writer encode those places. Device: whole pixels at ppem = round(size x 600 / 72) pixels per em (13.5 pt 113, 18 pt 150). A glyph after a space (a word start) goes to the pixel nearest its layout position measured from the glyph run's start (an exact half goes down below 1024 px and up from there). Any other glyph follows the one before by that glyph's advance in whole pixels (round(advance x ppem)) plus its kerning in whole pixels, moved back a pixel at a time while it is more than 17.5 cells (3.5 px) ahead of its layout position, and on a pixel at a time while its end (its start plus its own pixel advance) is 27.5 cells (5.5 px) or more short of the next glyph's layout position. PDF writer: draws each glyph by its PDF width W (1/1000 em: the advance x 1000 rounded to 1/64 and then to a whole unit, so Calibri i and l are 230 for 229.49) at the PDF font size Tf: 5 x ppem cells stretched down the slide from the baseline as the baseline is (K5), round((y + 5 ppem)(1 + s)) - round(y (1 + s)) cells for a baseline y cells down before the stretch, so 13.5 pt is 13.56 and in about one line in eight 13.584. It adds up (device advance, with I-027's extra cells, minus W x Tf / 1000) in units of Tf / 1000 since its last adjustment; when the sum reaches 3 units either way it writes an adjustment of the sum less a half, cut towards zero, before the next glyph and starts again from zero. The remainder it drops is the shortfall: 0.27 per mille at 13.5 pt, 0.5 at 18 pt, 1.3 at 12.75 pt. Spaces before a run's first other glyph are not in the PDF's text: that glyph starts it where the device puts it. On lines of one glyph repeated the PDF also uses a Tc.

issues.title: Long lines drift from PowerPoint's by up to 1.6 pt along their length: PowerPoint's PDF draws some glyph runs one 1/3000-inch step per glyph longer than its layout, depending on where the run starts on that grid
issues.fixed_in: sdkjs d90da7a1d0 (fix(slide): draw text on PowerPoint's PDF glyph grid)
issues.description: Found by the slide-by-slide comparison of the 1646-slide deck (a later version of the 838-slide deck: 377 slides the same, 75 with changed text, 1194 new), run k6-c. Every one of the 28138 lines paired by text between the two PDFs sits on PowerPoint's baseline (all within 0.124 pt, 28121 within 0.03 pt) and starts where PowerPoint's starts (within 0.33 pt), but the lengths differ: of the 16766 paired lines at least 300 pt long, 1238 differ by more than 0.5 pt and 312 by more than 1 pt (308 of them shorter in Euro-Office). At the review's 800 px a 1 to 1.6 pt drift moves the second half of a line by 1 to 2 px, and this is the main difference left on the deck: the 93 slides with a line more than 1 pt off average SSIM 0.958 (15 0.815, 39 0.829, 1283 0.855, 35 0.855, 38 0.863, 1371 0.901, 1487 0.906, 551 0.913, 1590 0.914), and the 525 slides whose lines all match within 0.3 pt average 0.997. Of the 120 slides under 0.98, 96 have a line more than 0.6 pt off and the rest 0.4 to 0.6 pt. The deck's three line breaks that differ on slides 15, 906 and 1308 turned out not to be part of this (see I-028). The 838-slide deck is mostly 13.5 pt text, where PowerPoint keeps to the layout on 82% of long lines, so its review saw only the edge of this (slide 255's 12.75 pt text about 0.1% long, slide 93's 'like').
issues.powerpoint: Lays text out with K2's model (its line breaks follow the model), but draws it on the PDF's 1/3000-inch grid (one cell, 0.024 pt) in runs of glyphs, and some runs come out longer than the layout. A layout position x (in cells from the slide's left edge) is drawn at P = x x (1 + a) + b, with a = 1.48323e-4 and b = 0.0304 cells on 720 x 540 pt slides and a = 1.28602e-4 and b = 0.0311 on 960 x 540 (fitted on boxes moved in 1-EMU steps; this is the 0.12 pt stretch of line starts I-024 first measured). A glyph run starts at P rounded to the nearest cell, which leaves a phase s, the sixteenths of a cell P lies past that cell (floor(16 P) - 16 x the cell, -8 to 7). Each glyph of the run then advances its layout width plus floor((s + 8 + round(16 x n x a)) / 16) cells, n being the glyph's layout width in cells: at s = 7 every glyph at least about 5.06 pt wide adds one cell to everything after it, at s = 6 every glyph at least about 15 pt wide, and at lower phases none at text sizes. The phase is the run's own and is not carried from glyph to glyph (only leading spaces at a line's start carry it into the first glyph). A 60-glyph run at s = 7 is thus about 1.4 pt longer than its layout, and the next line of the same paragraph, starting at another phase, may not be: this is the variation between lines of one run (slide 1283). A glyph run restarts at each a:r (except that an a:r of only spaces continues into the next), before and after a hyphen, en dash or em dash (the deck draws every hyphen alone), at tabs, pictures and equations, and at each line; spaces in the middle of a line that open a run restart it at its first visible glyph. The extra cells are only drawn on left, justified and distributed lines, and not in a run with character spacing (PowerPoint draws those with Tc), nor in the run after a hyphen or dash, after a space in the middle of a line, or after leading spaces in the middle of a line. Left and justified lines start at their indent rounded to the nearest 1/600 inch, and the text after a bullet starts at its own rounded marL.
issues.euro_office: Before the fix: drew every glyph at its layout position (K2), so each line came out at its layout length; on the 1646-slide deck 1237 of 16765 lines at least 300 pt long differed from PowerPoint's in length by more than 0.5 pt and 311 by more than 1 pt (median, Euro-Office minus PowerPoint, per mille of the length, by PowerPoint's Tf: Calibri 17.04 -0.51, 20.04 -1.41, 24.96 -1.50, 26.04 -2.32, 32.04 -1.29). Now, for slides of 720 x 540 or 960 x 540 pt with text that is not rotated or skewed and runs left to right, draws as PowerPoint's PDF does: each glyph run starts on the stretched grid with its phase, its glyphs get PowerPoint's extra cells, and left and justified indents are rounded to 1/600 inch. Line breaks are unchanged: this is drawing only. After the fix 596 of those lines differ by more than 0.5 pt and 30 by more than 1 pt (17.04 +0.55, 20.04 +0.73, 24.96 +0.76, 26.04 -0.05, 32.04 +0.42; what is left is I-024).
issues.suspected_cause: Cause found: PowerPoint's PDF export positions glyphs on its 1/3000-inch grid run by run, from a start that is its layout position stretched about the slide's left edge, and a run whose start lies 7/16 of a cell (or 6/16, for wide glyphs) past the cell it rounds to gains a cell per glyph from the stretch. It looks like a fixed-point step in sixteenths of a cell that adds each glyph's stretch to the start's fraction instead of the running one (a guess). K2's model holds for the layout and the line breaks; Euro-Office's line lengths differed only in drawing.

issues.title: Picture colour effects (clrChange, duotone, lum) ignored
issues.fixed_in: sdkjs 429072eb3f (fix(slide): apply picture colour change, brightness/contrast and duotone)
issues.description: Found by the 3963-slide deck's review (run i024-c, sdkjs f53e0a4a15). Blip effects inside a:blip are parsed but not applied when drawing. 1484: clrChange makes white (and red ED1C24) transparent; Euro-Office keeps them, so the map's white background covers the top of the caption. 1046/1047: clrChange black-to-transparent plus a red duotone; Euro-Office shows black squares around the moons and the moon is not red. 2902 and 2906: a:lum contrast 20000 / 10000; PowerPoint's pictures have visibly higher contrast (measured 1.10-1.26x stretch on 2906). Slides (5): 1046-1047, 1484, 2902, 2906.
issues.powerpoint: Bakes the effects into the picture's pixels. Every clrChange comes first and is matched against the original pixels, wherever it stands in the blip: a pixel within 1 of clrFrom in each channel takes clrTo's colour and alpha (clrTo with alpha 0 makes it transparent; 50% gives alpha 128). Then lum and duotone apply in the order the blip lists them. lum maps each channel v (0 to 1) to floor(255 x clip(k x (v - 1/2) + 1/2 + bright x (1 + k) / 2)), with k = 1 / (1 - contrast) for a positive contrast and 1 + contrast otherwise, so brightness alone adds and contrast alone pivots about mid-grey. duotone takes g = floor(0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B) of the sRGB values and gives round(c1 + (c2 - c1) x g / 255) per channel; its colours are worked out with their modifiers as for any colour (tint in linear light, satMod in HSL without capping the saturation: FF0000 tint 45% satMod 400% is (255, 107, 107)). The moon on 1046: black made transparent, then a black-to-light-red duotone, then lum bright 14% contrast 52%, so grey 128 becomes (183, 29, 29). The PDF holds the result as the picture's image, with a soft mask where it is transparent, encoded by K6's rule. Measured on the test deck blipfx-rules (lum sweeps, duotones, colour keys and orders on lossless ramps, exact to the level).
issues.euro_office: Before the fix: drew the original picture (only alphaModFix was honoured). Now, in slides, a picture or picture fill whose blip has clrChange, lum or duotone is drawn from a copy with PowerPoint's rules applied: the PDF path decodes the media file in x2t, applies the effects and passes the result to the writer as a PNG; the canvas path does the same from the loaded image. Results are cached per picture and effects. On the test deck every lossless image equals PowerPoint's to the level, and the JPEG ones differ by compression noise only.
issues.suspected_cause: Cause found: CBlipFill.Effects holds CClrChange, CDuotone and CLumEffect, but drawing only used CAlphaModFix (CBlipFill.getTransparent); nothing transformed the pixels, and picture brushes never worked out the effects' colours.

Presentation editor only; SVG, EMF and WMF pictures are left alone.

issues.title: scene3d camera rotation ignored (picture not mirrored)
issues.fixed_in: sdkjs 1587814993 (fix(slide): draw flat objects as their scene3d camera sees them)
issues.description: Found by the 3963-slide deck's review (run i024-c, sdkjs f53e0a4a15). Pictures with spPr scene3d camera orthographicFront and rot lon=10800000 (180 degrees about the vertical axis, 931 has 10799977) are shown mirrored left-right by PowerPoint. Euro-Office draws them unmirrored. 931 SSIM 0.747; 1046 0.929 (also N-02). Slides (2): 931, 1046.
issues.powerpoint: Draws a flat object (no sp3d) with a scene3d camera as the camera sees it, picture, geometry, outline and text alike. In the object's own frame, about its centre and after its flips (y down), the camera maps (u, v) to x = u cos(lon), y = u sin(lon) sin(lat) + v cos(lat), then turns the result counter-clockwise by rev; the object's rotation applies after that. So lon 180 mirrors it left to right and lat 180 top to bottom (text reads mirrored), both together or rev 180 turn it half round, and other angles foreshorten it; seen edge-on (lon or lat 90) it is not drawn. perspectiveFront gives the same result at lon 180, and at lon 60 its quadrants land in the same places. The PDF holds the result as an image rasterised at about 201.6 dpi with a soft mask, about 0.42 pt larger than the object. With lightRig threePt from the top, a square-on face is lit: the front face (lon and lat 0 or both 180) maps each colour channel v to round(1.03894 v + 5.007), the back face (exactly one of them 180) to round(0.77354 v + 9.984), both clipped to 0-255, on pictures and fills alike (4472C4 becomes (76, 123, 209) in front and (63, 98, 162) behind; 808080 becomes 138). A tilted face keeps the slope and gets a larger offset (lat 60: about 29; lat 300: about 44; lon 60: about 1). Measured on the test deck scene3d-rules (86 cases: camera angles, flips and rotations, an arrow, outlines, text, perspectiveFront, and lossless grey steps for the light).
issues.euro_office: Before the fix: scene3d was skipped when reading, so the object was drawn as stored. Now, in slides, scene3d is read into the shape's properties, and a shape, picture or connector whose camera is orthographicFront or perspectiveFront is drawn through the camera's map, inserted between its flips and its rotation: everything it draws (fill, outline, text, picture) moves with it, and nothing is drawn edge-on. A picture fill on a square-on face under threePt from the top gets PowerPoint's light, baked in after the picture's colour effects (I-030). On the test deck every picture case puts each quadrant where PowerPoint does, the shape and text cases match, and the square-on light fits PowerPoint's to the level (front 1.0390 v + 4.99, back 0.7735 v + 9.99).
issues.suspected_cause: Cause found: the PPTY spPr reader skipped record 5 (scene3d), so the camera never reached the shape model (only theme effect styles and SmartArt data read scene3d).
issues.code_area: sdkjs common/Shapes/Serialize.js ReadSpPr (scene3d read into CSpPr.scene3d as an AscFormat.Scene3d, outside the history; common/Drawings/Format/Format.js CSpPr copies it). common/Drawings/Format/GraphicObjectBase.js: drawWithSlideCamera (getSlideScene3dCamera, getSlideCameraMap) moves the object's transforms by base^-1 L base for one draw, L being the camera's map through the flips about the centre; getSlideSceneLighting adds the light to the picture's colour effects. Called at the top of CShape.draw (Shape.js) and CImageShape.draw (Image.js); word/Drawing/ShapeDrawer.js getBlipEffectsImage also takes a picture fill with scene3d. Presentation editor only.
issues.fix_idea: Done (see euro_office). Not done: the light on fills, outlines and text (I-038 has the rule), on tilted faces, and for other rigs or a rotated rig; other camera presets (oblique, isometric, perspective other than front); sp3d (bevels, extrusion); the camera on a group; PowerPoint's rasterising of the result (the PDF keeps vectors and text). scene3d is not written back when saving.
doubts: perspectiveFront is drawn as orthographic; PowerPoint's perspective was only compared at lon 180 (the same) and lon 60 (the quadrants land where the orthographic map puts them; the edges were not measured).
Hit testing and text editing still use the object's own frame, so a mirrored text box is edited unmirrored.

rejected.reason: Not a Euro-Office error. The outline has an explicit w=9525, and Euro-Office's PDF strokes the exact geometry (rect bottom at PDF y 140.24523 pt, width 0.74999). PowerPoint's own PDF export rounds the rect origin to 0.01 pt ('132.75 140.25 459 29.081 re'). That 0.0048 pt (0.01 device px) shift puts the stroke edge exactly on a device-pixel centre, so the shared Windows.Data.Pdf rasterizer lights row 887 for PowerPoint and not for Euro-Office. This is rounding in the reference PDF at a pixel-centre tie, not a rendering rule Euro-Office could fix.

Not a Euro-Office error. Euro-Office writes the 2.25 pt frame (explicit w=28575) exactly: top at PDF y 387.00003 = EMU 1943100. PowerPoint's PDF writes '546.34 295.38 79.158 91.618 re', so its top lands at 386.998 because the origin is rounded to 0.01 pt. The ideal stroke edge falls exactly on a device-pixel centre (hires 337.5), so a 0.002 pt rounding in the reference decides which row lights. Both PDFs go through the same rasterizer, so this is a tie broken by the reference's coordinate rounding, not an Euro-Office rendering rule.
